newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln Mark VIII dubbed most washable car.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln Mark VIII dubbed most washable car.

text.p: People who plan to spend a lot of time in car washes this year may want to consider the 1997 Lincoln Mark VIII.
Ford Motor Co.'s luxury coupe was named "America's Most Washable Car" by the Michigan Carwash Association Tuesday. Coming in second was the elliptically designed Ford Taurus.
General Motors Corp.'s Chevrolet Caprice, another smooth-cornered vehicle, tied for third with GM's Pontiac Grand Am.
What does it take to be one of the 12 vehicles nominated by the association's members?
"Professional washes do their best work on aerodynamic cars, which allow easy access to all exterior areas," said Bill Gill, executive director of the association.
That means cars should be free of indentations, have wheel wells that release dirt and debris easily, and securely attached mouldings and bumpers.

The Mark VIII will be featured on the cover of the February issue of Professional Carwashing & Detailing, a trade magazine out of Latham, N.Y. The headline for the article is "Lincoln - What a Washable Car Should Be," a takeoff on the Lincoln advertising slogan.

This is Ford's second washable crown. The Taurus won during the first year of the contest in 1993. The 1996 title went to GM's Cadillac Seville Touring Sedan. GM's Oldsmobile Aurora won in 1995, and Chrysler Corp.'s Dodge Intrepid in 1994.
